newsitem.title: USA: Owens-Illinois says profits up 11 pct in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Owens-Illinois says profits up 11 pct in quarter.

text.p: Owens-Illinois Inc., the maker of plastic and glass containers, said Thursday its earnings rose 11 percent in the fourth quarter, capping a year of record profits.
The company also announced that it completed its acquisition of some of the assets of Anchor Glass Container Corp., for about $125 million.

Owens-Illinois said it earned $22.9 million, or 19 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, compared with year earlier earnings of $20.7 million, or 17 cents a share. Sales were up 8 percent to $962.1 million from $892.4 million.
For the 1996 year, it posted record earnings of $191.1 million, or $1.58 a share, vs. 1995 earnings of $169.1 million, or $1.40 a share. Sales increased to $3.84 billion from $3.76 billion.
The company said its earnings were boosted by strong results from its U.S. glass container business and international operations.

"We are looking forward to another strong year in 1997, driven by improved performances in our existing businesses combined with the contributions of our recently completed acquisitions in Europe and the U.S.," said Joseph H. Lemieux, chairman and chief executive officer.

The company said it acquired Anchor Glass Container's glass container manufacturing plants in Antioch and Hayward, Calif. for $125 million. As part of the buyout, it will assume contractual agreements with Adolph Coors Co.'s Coors Brewing Co. and a stake in the Rocky Mountain Bottle Co.
Last week, Owens-Illinois also announced the acquisition of a controlling stake in AVIR S.p.A., Italy's largest glass container maker.
Owens-Illinois' stock was off 12.5 cents at $24.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
